G01.security_impact: Mixed, not a net improvement, and one sub-claim points the wrong way. Real improvement: two of the three live bundles record no 152-ФЗ consent at all today because every submit is rejected at the relay before reaching Maya, so a merge onto a live write creates records where none currently exist. But which write is not settled: this group's own PROPOSED SUCCESSOR names `/api/consent/submit` (aiohttp, webhook_server.py:10015, bot SQLite), while app.html uses `/client-channel/consent` (NestJS, client-channel.controller.ts:121, Postgres). These are different systems in different stores and are not interchangeable; asserting the consolidation direction as decided overstates what has been approved. Direction error to correct: retiring the legacy `401 → _unauth → done = true` branch (app-tenant.html:12219-12232) is presented as closing a fail-open, but the component being consolidated onto fails open wider and without recovery. AMayaConsent sets `checkedSession = signature` BEFORE the status fetch and does not reset it in the `.catch`, which does `setShow(false)`; `meWidgetAf`'s `finalize` throws on any `!r.ok`, so one 500/503/network blip on `/client-channel/status` suppresses the gate for the rest of that token's life, because the 800ms interval short-circuits on `checkedSession === signature`. Correction to the staff-exemption claim: `window.__meCurMode === 'staff'` is a property of the two legacy copies only (app-tenant.html:12208, maya-os-site:22047) and has zero relevance in the successor's base — AMayaConsent gates on `meAppAccessCurrentMode() !== 'client'`, `__meAppMode` is resolved only from the server's `app_access` contract («Persist only a server-returned mode», app.html:5680-5707), and eligibility is decided by the server's `/client-channel/status`. Finally, nothing here may promise a Telegram-channel consent write: Gate G20 requires «consents written on channel identity alone 0», and bot.py:1751 records that a Telegram callback identifies a channel, not a Client.
G01.objection: The security field calls retiring the legacy `401 → _unauth → done = true` branch an improvement, but the component it consolidates onto fails open strictly wider and never recovers. AMayaConsent assigns `checkedSession = signature` before the `/client-channel/status` fetch and does not reset it in the `.catch`, which calls `setShow(false)`; `meWidgetAf`'s `finalize` throws on any non-2xx, so a single 500/503/network error permanently suppresses the consent gate for that token's lifetime — the 800ms re-check short-circuits on `checkedSession === signature`. The legacy gate fails open only on an explicit 401 and resets `checkedRef.current = false` on 5xx/network, retrying every 800ms. So the merge does not retire a fail-open; it trades a narrow recoverable one for a broad permanent one. That is the most dangerous error class — a risk described as an improvement — and it is compounded by the field naming `/client-channel/consent` as the consolidation target when the group's own PROPOSED SUCCESSOR names `/api/consent/submit`, a different backend writing a different database.

G02.security_impact: The merge does not by itself weaken authority, but the original's reasoning for that is wrong in two places and its risk list is incomplete. The server-side gate is real and is not the only one: `team-communications.controller.ts` carries `@TenantScoped()` plus `@Roles(TENANT_OWNER, BUSINESS_OWNER, TENANT_ADMIN, ADMINISTRATOR, STAFF)` (S-272) and every handler scopes on `a.tenantId!`, and the МЭ relay path re-checks the same role set in `canonical_team_communications.handle` before forwarding the caller's own bearer to port 3107 — so authority ultimately rests with the controller, but "the only load-bearing check" is inaccurate. Note the gate's shape: STAFF and every owner/admin role share one tenant-wide feed, so this is role-gating, not separation of duties; it does not become weaker, but it was never fine-grained. The claim that "the merge re-parents UI, not that gate" is contradicted by the evidence it cites: S-100 states explicitly that a merge here "is a rebuild, not a re-parent," because ATeamChat's rich client (hold-to-record with slide-to-cancel and swipe-up lock, chunked attachments with per-chunk receipt verification, media viewer, presence/typing, TCVoice playback) has no counterpart in AChat. Four things must be engineered, not assumed. (1) Lane role scope: what keeps staff traffic out of a client's view today is partly that staff chat is a physically separate screen or build, so the lane selector must inherit the server role scope or internal messages surface in a client's thread (S-272). (2) Provenance: that same separation is what stops a master pasting client PD into a thread they believe is internal; once the human lane and the MAYA lane share one shell, visible human-vs-assistant provenance becomes the 152-ФЗ control, not a cosmetic detail (S-142). (3) Voice-path substitution — omitted by the original and a real 152-ФЗ direction change: the team recorder stores audio, the composer mic yields a transcript, so folding staff voice notes into the composer path would route staff speech (which can name clients) through a transcription/LLM pipeline the internal lane deliberately avoids (S-282). (4) Live microphone: S-282 records that streams are torn down on unmount (L38314) and that hosting the recorder in a chat lane that mounts and unmounts with messages risks leaking a live mic — a privacy regression created by the merge itself. On multi-tenancy the original understates the gap and mislabels it as an optional upgrade: it is not only the `maya-os-site` copy on the legacy proxy — `app-tenant.html`, the tenant build, routes its primary-nav staff team tab through the same single-tenant `TC_PROXY` (L21008), and since R12 retired the PHP storage owner both copies get HTTP 410 `canonical_team_owner_required`. So for those two builds this is repair of a dead, un-tenant-scoped surface onto the `@TenantScoped` controller, not a bonus improvement available by re-routing; skipping it leaves them broken rather than merely leaky. No frozen limitation is contradicted (no claim is made about fail-closed 13/21, STEP_UP, Gate 10, approval separation-of-duties, or GAP-ATTENDANCE-CONFIRM).

(2) "No client-side check that was load-bearing is removed" gets the direction wrong. saasIsCalManager() (L14020) is today the only thing keeping the journal and its per-master pill off a provider/employee/staff screen, and the CRM read path this widget takes for external-CRM tenants (L12623-12624) is gated by CRM_JOURNAL_ROLES, which deliberately includes PROVIDER, EMPLOYEE and STAFF (crm-integration.controller.ts L52-62), while getJournal passes query.providerId straight to the adapter with no per-actor fence (crm.service.ts L3212) — the write path has assertJournalStaffWritable, the read path has no counterpart. The API already admits a shift master reading a colleague's book, so this is not a new privilege; but re-parenting the widget to a chat-reachable capability converts a latent API permission into a one-utterance control, through exactly the pill row S-543 describes. G05 should therefore carry the condition G06 carries: no re-parenting ahead of a server-side authority gate on the journal read. The internal-calendar path is unaffected (INTERNAL_CALENDAR_MANAGER_ROLES excludes staff roles). Neither claim contradicts a frozen limitation — and the fail-closed posture is why this matters: the server-side authority gate is NORMATIVE-PENDING, so the client test is currently the only one holding.
G05.objection: The security field calls a conditional risk "NONE", which is the most dangerous error class. S-543's pill sets &providerId on a read the server does not fence per-actor: getJournal (crm.service.ts L3212) forwards query.providerId to the adapter with no counterpart to the write path's assertJournalStaffWritable, and CRM_JOURNAL_ROLES deliberately admits PROVIDER/EMPLOYEE/STAFF. The only thing keeping that pill off a shift master's screen today is the client-side saasIsCalManager() test at app.html L14020 — precisely the kind of check the proposal says is "not load-bearing". The API permission pre-exists, so this is exposure surfacing rather than privilege escalation, but a dossier entry that says NONE gives a reviewer no reason to demand the server gate before the re-parenting ships. Secondary: the entry's headline user claim ("the one difference a user would actually see") survives on its own terms — I confirmed L14226 precedes the toolbar at L14254 and the «раздел интеграций» copy renders no link — but it is stated as the only difference while the evidence rows it cites name two more (the filter's loadMyStaff orphaning in S-543, the retry-on-unretryable-code flattening in S-545), both of which cut against the merge. Selecting the one favourable difference and calling it the only one is the padding in this entry.

G06.user_impact: The owner and the masters/managers who share the legacy panel notice this one — but only on the legacy single-salon branch. ALivePanel's first statement (app.html L34904 / maya-os-site L31557) hands SaaS manager roles to ASaasOwnerPanel, so a tenant manager already sees the nine-tab SaaS panel today; the ten-tab strip — Аналитика, Расписание, Отчёт, Лист ожидания, Отзывы, Задачи, Рассылка, Команда, Гашение plus the founder-only MAYA tab — is what the live salon on the legacy proxy sees, and it is permission-filtered, so only a founder-owner ever sees all ten (app.html's `avail` filter L37174-37182 shows Аналитика unconditionally and gives any owner every tab). Afterwards there is no strip, and each capability is asked for in chat. The real, felt risk is the contents, not the container: six of those tabs (report, waitlist, reviews, jobs, broadcast, redeem) have no counterpart in ASaasOwnerPanel's TABS (L30829-30838), so if the merge target is taken to be the SaaS panel the owner loses the eight-job lifecycle-marketing catalogue and the code-redemption counter path. Honest calibration: three of the six are already part-notional, not two. The `panel_job_run` action (POST /api/panel/job/run) answers 410 with a canonical pointer; /api/panel/team mode=list returns an empty roster with a "canonical_action" pointer and every other mode 410s; and /api/panel/redeem still looks a code up but refuses mode=confirm with 409 «Погашение через старый контур отключено» — the counter can check a code and cannot redeem it. The renderOS() claim holds for S-030 only: in app.html the full-screen `god` route now renders Расходы alone, so the embedded panel tab is the sole reachable renderOS(); in maya-os-site (S-096) the god screen still defaults to its own `os` tab and stays reachable via ?god=1 and the MAYA alert card. And "comes back as a contract-declared widget" is contingent, not given — any of these keys left unmapped or `restricted` derives a STEP_UP_VERIFIED floor, which is unreachable, so it is withheld rather than re-surfaced.
G06.security_impact: Direction is half right. Deleting the container alone is neutral: the client-side filters are visibility filters over a permissions object the server itself issued at /api/panel/me (`__meIsFounder` from is_platform_owner/is_founder, role from canonical_staff_access.panel_role), and the legacy endpoints do re-authenticate and re-derive role — redeem → permissions.redeem 403, daily_report → role != 'owner' 403, reviews → permissions.reviews 403, waitlist and dashboard → permissions.analytics / permissions.dashboard 403, master/overview → is_master 403, the MAYA tab → `_god_gate` canonical-platform authority 403 — and app.html says so in its own comment above the filter («Сервер всё равно гейтит»). Two corrections to the evidence: it is not four tests but ten `show(p,i)` predicates (p.analytics, p.reviews, p.jobs, p.marketing, p.staff, p.redeem besides the four named) plus an `avail` filter that already overrides two of the four — analytics returns true unconditionally, and an owner gets every tab regardless of perms; and "every endpoint re-authenticates" is not literal, since panel_broadcast mode='templates' returns the catalogue before any `_panel_auth` and the client sends that mode with no auth header by design (app.html L35440-35441). salon_stats and salary are not behind these tabs at all — neither string appears in the frontend. The larger correction is "not checks a server gate must now be built to replace": true of the legacy contour, false of the successor, which is exactly why the dossier rates this MEDIUM-HIGH and approves only conditionally. `loyalty.legacy-redeem.execute.v1` and `gift-certificates.redemption.execute.v1` sit among the 164 of 221 canonical policy definitions carrying the permissive twelve-role TENANT_ACTION_ROLES default, and the broadcast tab's canonical contour carries GAP-BULK-SEND-DIRECT (`communication.bulk-campaign.execute.v1`: ALLOW, approvalRequirement NONE, twelve roles including CLIENT and CUSTOMER). Re-parenting redeem or broadcast onto those keys trades a stricter legacy gate for a weaker canonical one, and any approval on that path is role-gated, not separation-of-duties. Tenant scope remains genuinely open as stated, and nothing in these two rows touches consent records or audit trails.
G06.objection: The security field calls the group "NEUTRAL, verging on a small tidy-up" by auditing only the legacy endpoints, which is the wrong altitude for a MERGE disposition whose whole content is re-parenting. At the capability level the direction inverts for at least two tabs: the legacy `permissions.redeem` 403 is stricter than the canonical redemption keys it would move to (both on the permissive twelve-role TENANT_ACTION_ROLES default, 164 of 221), and the broadcast tab's canonical contour carries an ungated second door onto the bulk send (ALLOW, approvalRequirement NONE, CLIENT and CUSTOMER among the allowed actor roles). Asserting "not checks a server gate must now be built to replace" therefore retires the dossier's own approval condition on evidence that does not cover the step where the condition applies — the classic and most dangerous error of reading a risk as a tidy-up.

G07.user_impact: The owner signing up notices most, and the specific thing they notice is that the starting door decides the product. There are not two copies but four across three bundles: the app.html login wizard (S-008), the app.html in-app owner wizard (S-285), the ALogin copy in maya-os-site (S-075), and the AChat copy in the same file that S-285 names as a third to reconcile. The differences run in BOTH directions, so "in-app is the superset" is only true within app.html: the login copy alone has the manual, non-conversational fallback form (lgManual L6283) — the very fallback the chat-first constraint requires — and the trial sheet alone has the locked state (lgTrialLocked L6780) and the ?trial=1 / ?start=trial marketing entries, while the paywall sheet it pairs with owns checkout and post-payment re-validation (S-007); the in-app copy alone survives reload, owns CRM branch discovery/search/import and the "Данные из CRM · подтверждены" confirm block (S-285); and in maya-os-site the ALogin copy owns the CRM provider picker and logo upload while the AChat copy owns weekly-schedule capture (WK_ORDER L16164) (S-075). Logo is a stage in every copy — only the explicit skip affordance is in-app — so it is not a differentiator. Voice is likewise NOT a new benefit: all copies already accept spoken answers today through three separate STT paths (S-281, S-075); the merge changes the count of ingresses, not what the owner can do. What the owner actually gains is that the answer set, the resumability and the CRM import stop depending on where they started, and that trial activation and CRM connect become stages of one conversation. The platform operator notices second: "＋ Новый салон" is the only primary-nav row in this group and one of the 101 Maya-owned primary-nav entries that collapse to 5 (verified: 101 rows with primaryNav ∧ mayaOwned). But "becomes the same conversation asked with operator authority" is not reachable on today's substrate: the widget contract registers no onboarding or tenant-creation capability at all (0 hits), an unmapped key fails closed to STEP_UP_VERIFIED under §0.8 F50, and P-12 makes STEP_UP_VERIFIED unreachable — so until those keys are registered at a floor at or below SESSION_VERIFIED the operator path is at best a HANDOFF to a secure surface, not a chat-actuated stage. Staff and clients notice nothing here, but the scoping is pre-tenant (S-007, S-008, S-075), owner-scoped (S-281, S-285) and platform-operator-scoped (S-155, roleMode "platform") — not "pre-tenant or owner-scoped" — and the operator wizard's done screen, which hands one-time credentials for an account minted at role tenant_admin, still needs a home in the successor.
G07.security_impact: Direction is right: no authority gate is added or strengthened here, and the honest reading is added risk that server-side work must absorb. The only genuine gain is hygiene, not a closed hole — three STT ingresses and three credential-entry implementations collapsing to one removes places where the rules below can drift apart. Running one component across the @Public() onboarding routes with opaque draft tokens (S-281) and the authenticated path means the draft id/token — today in refs plus session-scoped storage, never URL or localStorage (S-285 L17528-17529, S-075 L5348) — must not be routed through any persisted chat transcript; S-075 names exactly that draft-token leak, and names it for the draft token only. The CRM-credential claim as proposed is false for half the merge and must be split: on the pre-tenant funnel the token is a type:'password' field that is genuinely never stored (verified in code — discoverDraftCrm and importDraftCrm pass dto.apiToken straight to the CRM preview and write no token field onto the draft), but the S-155 operator wizard being folded into the same conversation PATCH/POSTs that same token to /admin/tenants/{id}/crm, where crm.service.ts stores it as encryptedApiToken. One merged credential field would therefore carry two opposite persistence contracts, which is the drift the claim assumes away. The role-gate description is also misread: the actual decorators are @Roles(PLATFORM_OWNER) on POST /admin/tenants and on POST /admin/tenants/{id}/activate (both @TenantScoped), and @Roles(PLATFORM_OWNER, TENANT_ADMIN) + @TenantScoped + @RequiresQuota(STAFF) on POST /admin/tenants/{id}/users — where "role tenant_admin" is the DEFAULT ROLE OF THE ACCOUNT BEING CREATED (CreateTenantUserDto restricts it to TENANT_OWNER/TENANT_ADMIN/BRANCH_MANAGER/STAFF), not the caller gate. So "minting an admin user" is not new exposure: a tenant_admin can already do that inside its own tenant today, quota-bounded; the genuinely operator-only powers are tenant creation and "Активировать сразу · без триала". The "role-gated only, not separation-of-duties" tag must be dropped: that frozen limitation is about the approval path, where canDecide resolves approvalPolicy 'owner' to any owner-role member including the initiator, and S-155 says nothing about it. These endpoints exclude tenant roles from /activate outright, which is a role-boundary gate, not a four-eyes gate; what the merge removes is bundle-level defence in depth — operator-only branches stop living in a separate admin bundle a tenant never loads — leaving that server-side gate as the sole barrier. Two further server-side obligations belong here: converging the onboarding voice ingress must not redirect it onto the bearer-authenticated @TenantScoped() /ai/transcribe, because onboarding is pre-tenant and holds no tenant token, which would break onboarding voice entirely (S-281); and any operator-authority tenant create/activate offered in chat needs its capability key registered, since an unregistered key fails closed to the unreachable STEP_UP_VERIFIED (§0.8 F50, P-12) and a key registered at risk tier 'restricted' is permanently withheld.
G07.objection: The CRM-token sentence states a protective property that holds for only one of the two surfaces being merged. "A type:'password' field the backend explicitly does not persist" is true of the @Public() onboarding funnel — the evidence itself scopes it to discovery (onboarding.controller.ts L106-108), and the code confirms neither discover nor import writes the token onto the draft. But S-155, the other half of this merge, sends the operator's CRM token to /admin/tenants/{id}/crm, where crm.service.ts persists it as encryptedApiToken. The claim therefore uses the safer surface's property to describe a component that will also carry the persisting one, which is precisely the kind of drift a merge causes rather than prevents. The second-strongest objection is adjacent: the text reads "role tenant_admin" — the role of the account the wizard CREATES — as the caller-side gate, and then imports the approval path's role-gated-not-separation-of-duties limitation onto endpoints that are in fact @Roles(PLATFORM_OWNER) on create and activate. That inverts who is already able to do what (a tenant_admin can mint tenant users today) and over-claims weakness where the role boundary is the stronger control.

G08.user_impact: Two different people notice, and a third notices almost nothing. A prospective salon owner signing up today fills the seven-input trial form on `сайт и приложение/maya-start.html` (L69-81): brand name, auto-transliterated slug (L111-114), the schedule-source radio (internal MAYA calendar vs external CRM, L72-73), e-mail, owner name, and optional phone and password. Branch name and the Europe/Moscow timezone are NOT inputs — they are derived and hardcoded at L148-149 and the owner is never asked; the proposed enumeration wrongly presents them as questions the conversation must take over, while omitting three fields it actually must (e-mail, owner name, phone). The flow does not end at "tenant created": the done screen renders a one-time `temporary_password` (L190) and auto-hands an owner session into maya-admin (L207-228), so the successor inherits a credential hand-off, not just a questionnaire. Note that the group carries an unresolved contradiction the owner is being asked to sign: S-159's own rationale keeps the typed form "as the fallback for exactness and for anyone who prefers typing fields", while G08's WHAT DISAPPEARS retires "the standalone trial form" — one of the two has to give. A barbershop client on `index.html` today taps any of four identical bare `t.me/malesthetic_bot` links (mobile nav L681, hero L834, footer L2665, exit-intent L5267) and lands in the bot with a generic handoff reply that knows nothing about where they came from; after the merge they meet one door instead of four. The "carries its origin" half is not delivered by this group — nothing in it builds a payload consumer, and an origin-carrying payload scheme already exists in the deployed bot (`ref_<code>`, bot.py L648). A visitor to `maya-site.html` notices nothing in the CTAs: S-169 is a verbatim repeat of the hero block — the demo URL at L397 is byte-identical to L245 — so collapsing it removes a duplicate, not a capability. But the row is "Final CTA + footer", and the footer at L404-409 carries the non-duplicate compliance line «Платформа для салонов и барбершопов · Сделано в России · 152-ФЗ»; "notices nothing at all" holds only if that line survives the merge.
G08.security_impact: No client-side authority check is removed: all three rows are pre-login entry points reachable without auth (roleMode any/any/client, primaryNav false), and tenant creation on S-159 is a server decision — so on the "removed check" axis this group is NEUTRAL. But S-159 is not otherwise security-quiet, and the proposed text spends its paragraph on the wrong hazards. Correcting the direction: the 409 slug-taken and 429 auth_rate_limited handling (L160-168) are NOT "the only uniqueness and anti-abuse guards" — both statuses are issued by the server on POST /onboarding/trial; the page only rewrites the 409 into Russian and runs a local countdown seeded from the server's own Retry-After. A conversational path that drops them loses error legibility, not abuse control (the same is true of the client-side slug regex at L138); claiming it "weakens abuse control on tenant provisioning" manufactures a security loss and contradicts this paragraph's own "already a server decision" clause. The real S-159 obligations are two. First, transcript containment is broader than the password: the password is optional (L81, "пусто — сгенерируем"), so the clean answer is for the conversation never to ask for one — but the completion step renders a one-time `temporary_password` (L190) and writes an owner `access_token` + `refresh_token` bundle into localStorage under a nonce key for hand-off to maya-admin (L207-228), and none of that may become chat content. Second, and unmentioned: L101 takes the API base from a `?api=` URL parameter (falling back to localStorage, then `http://localhost:3000/api`) on an unauthenticated public page that then POSTs owner e-mail, name, phone and password to it — a crafted signup link redirects the entire payload to an arbitrary host and seeds the hand-off with whatever token bundle that host returns. This is pre-existing and the merge neither creates nor closes it, but the successor must not inherit a query-settable API base while also carrying credentials. On S-194, a payload scheme IS an improvement over four bare links — the evidence says so directly — and simultaneously a collision risk; the proposed text's "not an attribution or audit improvement" overcorrects into the opposite error. The collision surface is also larger and more valuable than the three cited rows: the deployed bot consumes `app_<nonce>` sign-in (bot.py L561), `linkphone` phone binding (L526), `redeem_<code>` certificate redemption (L638), `loy_<code>` loyalty-point redemption (L643), `ref_<code>` referral — which already writes state and grants both parties a discount (L648) — and exact-match `gift_cert` (L685). Two of those are staff redemption paths and one is already a marketing-attribution write, so a new origin payload must be prefix-disjoint from all six, and `app_` in particular is prefix-matched (L561) so a colliding payload surfaces to the user as a bogus "sign-in link expired". Note that the identity-consent working copy of bot.py consumes only `app_` and leaves `linkphone`/`gift_cert` inert; the two trees disagree and the payload contract must be specified against the deployed one. Printed and shared bare links must keep resolving. Neither claim touches a frozen limitation: fail-closed counts, STEP_UP reachability, Gate 10 enforcement, approval role-gating and GAP-ATTENDANCE-CONFIRM all live in the post-login widget contract, and none of these three surfaces reaches it.
G08.objection: The security claim inverts one direction and then misses the row's actual hazard. It asserts that dropping S-159's 409/429 handling "weakens abuse control on tenant provisioning" — but maya-start.html L160-168 shows both statuses arrive FROM the server (the 429 countdown is explicitly seeded from the server's Retry-After, and the code comment says so); the page only renders them. Dropping them degrades error messaging, and the paragraph contradicts itself two clauses earlier by conceding tenant creation "is already a server decision". Because that invented risk occupies the S-159 slot, the genuine one goes unnamed: L101 reads the API base from a `?api=` query parameter on a public unauthenticated page, and the form then POSTs ownerEmail, ownerName, ownerPhone and password there and writes the returned access/refresh token bundle into localStorage for hand-off into maya-admin (L207-228). A crafted "start your trial" link therefore exfiltrates the signup payload and seeds an attacker-supplied owner session — which is exactly the kind of thing a security paragraph on this row exists to surface, and it is precisely the marketing-link context this group is about to consolidate.

G09.user_impact: Who notices depends on auth state and bundle, not on role. **The splash is a logged-out surface, not a universal one.** The white MAYA logo screen (S-003 — `MayaSplash`, app.html L15870: 2300 ms hold + 300 ms fade, 700 ms under prefers-reduced-motion, tap anywhere to skip, once per browser session via sessionStorage `me_maya_mark_splash`) is a render state of ALogin (`lgSplash` L6340, early return L8195). MEApp's initial screen resolves from the stored `me_saas_auth_v2:<ns>` bundle straight to home / staff-home / panel / god / access-compat (L38578-38640), so a signed-in user never mounts ALogin and never sees it; a legacy Telegram-token user does start at `login`, but meAuthRoute's boot poll routes them away in ~50-100 ms (L41582), so they see a flash, not 2.3 s. It is also app.html-only: app-tenant.html has no splash at all (0 hits for `lgSplash`/`MayaSplash`), and maya-os-site/index.html has a *different* one — 3200 ms, aurora backdrop, its own tap-to-skip (L5399-5415, L6871) — which belongs to S-073, not to this group, and survives this merge. Note also that S-003's row name («splash slide-to-unlock») conflates two separate things inside ALogin: the splash has no slide gesture, and the nearest real slide-to-unlock there is the trial-activation knob (`lgKnob` L6782, S-283 — KEEP AS CAPABILITY, with the exactly-once `lgTrialReq` guard), which must not be swept into this group by that wording. **The landing change is real but not new everywhere.** After login users stop arriving at a role-picked screen — client home, the «Я клиент / Я сотрудник» chooser, staff-home / a business panel tab / god, or Integrations via `__meBootCrm` — and arrive in the chat thread instead. On maya-os-site a client already lands in Maya chat today by both the SaaS and the legacy path (`meSaasOpenMayaChat('client','home')`, L38251 / L38254 / L38274), and app.html's meAuthRoute carries a comment recording that client chat-landing was deliberately removed there (L41530-41531) — so for app.html clients this is the reversal of a recent product decision the owner should be told about, not a first-time gain. «Resume» is a K3/B21 deliverable, not today's behaviour: `meSaasOpenMayaChat` mints a fresh `__meChatVisitKey` on every open precisely so AChat remounts (index.html L4971), so the honest claim is "lands in the chat thread", with resume as the thing the successor must add. The chooser is not simply deleted either — the group's own WHAT WILL REMAIN keeps workspace selection, and the chooser is reached exactly when the workspace is ambiguous (`meSaasEffectiveWorkspace` empty / `resolved.chooser`), which is the case the conditional approval requires the successor to ask about. **On the tenant bundle a client can lose their only way in.** «Войти через VK ID» is rendered and wired there (app-tenant.html L4026 → `loginVk` L22812); that bundle has no email login (`lgEmail` 0 hits) and no Yandex handler in boot (only `handleVkRedirect`, L23170), so S-614 leaves Telegram as the sole working login unless the merge adds Yandex as the row demands. For a VK-only client that is lost access, not a cosmetic change: no one's *permissions* change, but one population's ability to authenticate at all does.
G09.security_impact: Neutral on server authorization, with one risk the group itself rates MEDIUM and two carry-overs — not "mostly neutral" flat. The role meAuthRoute reads is cached: `app_access` on the server-issued user inside the `me_saas_auth_v2:<ns>` bundle, plus the client-written `me_is_staff` flag on the legacy path. It only picks a destination — `meAppAccessFetchAndRoute` / `panel_me` re-decide immediately and the server validates every token — so collapsing the routing table removes no authorization gate. **Carry-over 1, verified unique.** `__meDropForeignLogin()` has exactly one caller in all three bundles, the first line of `meAuthRoute` (index.html L38222, app.html L41489, app-tenant.html L23122); it is published on `window` but nothing else calls it, and nothing else anywhere compares `Telegram.WebApp.initDataUnsafe.user.id` against stored `tg_auth_data` (app.html has only two other `initDataUnsafe` hits, both avatar code). It is therefore the only code that drops a previous Telegram user's `tg_auth_data` + `web_session_token` when a different Telegram account opens the same Mini App webview (app.html L41368-41382) — and only inside Telegram, since it returns early without a live `initDataUnsafe.user`, so the exposure is a shared Telegram webview/device, not any shared browser. The server cannot replace it because it never sees the initDataUnsafe mismatch, so a resume path that does not call it leaves a prior user's still-valid legacy session live and sendable as a credential. **Carry-over 2, duplicated but still required.** The same SaaS branch of meAuthRoute is also the fail-closed entry (`meAppAccessEnterCompat` / `__meGo('access-compat')` when `app_access` cannot be resolved, L41511-41512), the place a 401 from /me clears the stored session (`meSaasClearStoredSession('me_unauthorized')`, L41516-41517), and the place the stored bundle is scoped to the loaded tenant (L41505 — which accepts a bundle carrying no `tenant_slug` for any slug, a weakness to fix rather than copy). These also exist in MEApp's copy (L38590, L38784-38785) and the fetch wrapper (L12241/12252/12268), so no single one is unique — but the stated point of this group is to collapse to one resolver, so whichever resolver survives must keep all three. The residual risk is the one the group already names and this field omitted: a resume that guesses a workspace or tenant lands a user in the wrong one, which the authority model forbids for effectful action. Dropping the VK `?code` return removes one of three writers into `web_session_token` in app.html (VK L40891, Yandex L40957, applogin poll L41220) and one of two in app-tenant (L22852, L22985) — a store that «Выйти на всех устройствах» does not clear (`revokeAllMySessions` → DELETE /auth/sessions → `saasLogout` → `saasForceLogout` → `saasClearSession` never touches it; only `__meLogout` L41567 does; S-604, S-605, S-578) — and it does not close that gap, because the Yandex path S-614 requires writes the same store.
G09.objection: The headline claim is falsified by the code it cites. "Every PWA user — client, staff and owner — notices the ~2.3-second splash" is false for exactly the users who matter most: the splash is a render state of ALogin (`lgSplash` app.html L6340, early return L8195), and MEApp's initial screen resolves from the stored `me_saas_auth_v2:<ns>` bundle to home/staff-home/panel/god/access-compat (L38578-38640), so a signed-in user never mounts ALogin. A legacy-token user starts at `login` but is routed away by the boot poll in ~50-100 ms (L41582). It is a logged-out, app.html-only experience — app-tenant.html has no splash, and maya-os-site's 3.2 s aurora splash (L5399-5415) is S-073 and is untouched by this group. That over-generalisation is precisely the "generic chat-first benefit pasted onto a group" failure mode. Second, and more decision-relevant for the owner: the landing change is not new. maya-os-site already lands clients in Maya chat on both paths (L38251/38254/38274), and app.html's meAuthRoute carries a comment stating that client chat-landing was deliberately removed there ("Раньше здесь открывался чат…", L41530-41531). G09 therefore re-does a decision this bundle consciously reversed, and neither the impact text nor the group's WHY says so — while "resume the conversation" is asserted as delivered behaviour when `meSaasOpenMayaChat` mints a fresh `__meChatVisitKey` per open (index.html L4971) specifically to remount AChat. Third, the last sentence contradicts its own paragraph: losing the only login method a VK-only tenant-bundle client has is a change in what they can do, not just "which login buttons exist".

G10.security_impact: Neutral for authority — no hole is closed and none is opened — and the claimed improvement does not survive counting. The role branch the RISK line names is correctly described as a destination chooser rather than a gate: `_pmSaasRole` is `meSaasCurrentRole()` → `bundle.user.role` out of the stored server-issued bundle, and it only picks which cabinet tab opens. But the inference drawn from that — that the screens it opens enforce their own access, so removing it needs no server-side check — is evidenced nowhere in S-048/S-111/S-176, which carry no backend evidence at all, and the visible destination repeats the same client-side test: the cabinet's tab list itself branches on `viewManager`, `saasIsStaffRole()` and `saasIsCalManager()` (app.html L13960-13982). The RISK line therefore stands as written — resolve the destination server-side AND confirm the destination's data endpoints authorize independently before dropping the branch; it may not be booked as already true. The consolidation improvement is miscounted: `cabinet_session` / `cabinet_me_login` are called from three bundles, not two (app.html L40124/40130/40136, `сайт и приложение/index.html` L5592-5593, `maya-os-site/index.html` L37031/37037), and G10 retires only the marketing overlay, leaving two client-cabinet implementations. It is also not a storage or attack-surface reduction: index.html and app.html share one origin and both read and write `web_session_token` in localStorage, so the token stays exactly where it was. Under frozen limitation 7 — Gate 10 is a shadow gate, "three front doors, one function" is measured, not enforced — this is a measurement, not a delivered control. Nothing here touches consent records, tenant isolation, STEP_UP (unreachable) or approval role-gating. The one regression is narrower than stated: dropping S-048's logout row removes the only sign-out affordance for a non-business client (business roles keep the cabinet «Сессии» tab and the owner panel), and it is an affordance loss only — server-side revocation and the multi-device revoke path are untouched.
G10.objection: The security field commits the exact direction error the review is meant to catch: it takes the group's own named RISK ("a client-side role test that must not be recreated") and discharges it as needing no replacement, on the unevidenced assertion that "the screens it opens enforce their own access" — an assertion that appears in none of the three cited surfaces and is contradicted in kind by the destination itself, whose cabinet tab list re-derives the same `bundle.user.role` client-side (app.html L13960-13982). Compounding this, the sole claimed improvement is arithmetically false — `cabinet_session`/`cabinet_me_login` have three callers, not two, so retiring S-176 leaves two implementations — and buys no security property at all, since index.html and app.html are the same origin and both persist `web_session_token` in the same localStorage. Net: a neutral-to-unverified change was written up as a closed risk plus an improvement.

G11.user_impact: Only the owner is affected, but not in the way stated: in the swept tree this console is already dead in the Telegram channel, so what the merge changes is a refusal becoming a capability, not a keyboard becoming words. `canonical_staff_access.current()` is populated only by the webhook server's aiohttp middleware (canonical_staff_access.py L156-198), and that module's own docstring states that native Telegram updates never acquire the context; bot.py never installs the middleware and never sets the ContextVar, so `is_admin()` is False for every Telegram update — `/admin` (L1281-1283) answers «Команда только для администраторов.» to the owner himself, and `_admin_dispatch` (L1298) refuses every `admin_cat_*`/`admin_run_*` tap. The folder walk (tap category → tap leaf → ← Назад) is what the code draws, not what the owner can reach; if the deployed VPS build predates the R02 cutover it may still hold there, so the entry must date the claim rather than assert it as today's behaviour. Parity is also overstated: the five keyboards carry 19 buttons / 18 distinct callbacks (`admin_run_cashiers` is cross-listed at L1232 and L1256), and at least six do not perform their action even with a valid principal — react/cycle/sub_now are `retention_owner_required` refusals (L1433-1442, L1070-1079, L1100-1109), reviews is a one-line app link (L3812-3813), ai_prov returns a `confirmation_link` URL (L1443-1450), and broadcast's send path `_broadcast_execute` (L3664-3668) returns `B35_CANONICAL_OWNER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED_USE_PANEL`. S-415's "low-risk, both already exist as commands" is wrong for a further reason: `_QueryAsUpdate` (L1266-1276) hands the category screen itself to the handler as `update.message`, so `cmd_broadcast` parses that screen's title «📣 Маркетинг и анонсы» as a text argument (L3573-3576) and the button skips the template menu entirely, opening a broadcast preview whose body is the menu label. Two pieces of context do vanish with the folders unless deliberately carried over — the line telling the owner these broadcasts already run on schedule (L1317-1319), and the Аналитика grouping together with its `# Аналитика (read-only)` comment (L1342), which is the only written record of which leaves only read. Clients are affected only by S-656, and the dead end is narrower than stated: while the opt-in screen is up the client is by definition still gated and `/unsubscribe` is not in `_GATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS` (L353), so the gate re-shows the consent screen and stops the update (L461-479); once they answer the marketing question, the same command reaches cmd_unsubscribe and returns an app-link redirect that revokes nothing in Telegram (L576-585). Either way the promise at L445 has no in-channel mechanism behind it, before the merge or after.
G11.security_impact: NEUTRAL for authority, but not for the reason given. The gate is `canonical_staff_access.is_admin` at bot.py L1298, and it resolves through a request-scoped canonical principal that only the webhook server's aiohttp middleware ever establishes — so in this channel it is not a removable duplicate; it is the only check standing, and it already refuses everyone, the owner included. The premise that "every leaf re-checks it independently" is false: 15 of the 18 handlers call `is_admin` themselves (cmd_ai_cost L1387, cmd_export_consents L1408, cmd_loyalty_backfill L3743 among them), but cmd_whats_new (L551), cmd_reviews_now (L3812) and cmd_ai_provider (L1443) do not, and for those three the L1298 dispatch gate is the only admin check on the button path. No hole opens — none of the three mutates anything (a client-facing release card, an app link, and a URL the governed-settings endpoint must authorize server-side) — but the blanket claim would license deleting a router gate that is load-bearing for three leaves. The backfill defect as described does not exist: `loyalty.run_backfill_job` (loyalty.py L786-794) opens with `return _legacy_loyalty_mutation_disabled('backfill_legacy_loyalty')`, which raises `LegacyLoyaltyCutoverError`; the accrual body beneath it is dead code, and the same cutover disables admin_run_loy_now (`run_loyalty_job` L553-555) and admin_run_ref_now (referral resolver refusal, referral.py L211+). A tap on admin_run_backfill accrues nothing — it would surface to the owner as «Ошибка: p4_03_legacy_mutation_disabled:…» via the handler's except (L3767-3770). Calling that an existing gap, and its confirmation an improvement, inverts the facts and invites the one genuinely dangerous move available in this group: reading the conditional approval ("each `admin_run_*` carries its contract-assigned confirmation before the keyboard goes") as licence to re-wire a mutation that P4-03 and B35 deliberately fail-closed. Re-enabling it behind a confirm dialog would reverse a fail-closed decision while presenting itself as a safety improvement. If one leaf deserves the unconfirmed-bulk-effect flag it is `admin_run_birthday`, which is not cut over: `birthday.run_birthday_job` still writes promo rows and publishes real Telegram deliveries through `maya_inbox_bridge.publish_inbox_item`. Any confirmation added anywhere here remains role-gated — the same admin asks and confirms — and must never be described as separation of duties. The live consent defect stands as S-656 states it: the marketing opt-in at L445 still promises «Согласие можно отозвать в любой момент командой /unsubscribe» while both commands are redirect-only (L576-585) and neither is in the gate allow-list (L353); the comment block at L348-350 still documents them as gate exceptions that the allow-list no longer grants. Fixing the copy or restoring in-channel revocation is a genuine improvement; leaving both as-is leaves the defect exactly where it stands.
G11.objection: The entry's one load-bearing risk claim is backwards, and the error is exploitable. It asserts that `admin_run_backfill` "fires a bulk welcome-points accrual across the whole client base on a single tap with no confirmation step" and that attaching the contract's confirmation "closes an existing gap". Neither half holds: `loyalty.run_backfill_job` returns `_legacy_loyalty_mutation_disabled('backfill_legacy_loyalty')` on its first executable line (loyalty.py L786-794) — the accrual is unreachable dead code — and the tap cannot pass `is_admin` at all, because native Telegram updates never acquire a canonical principal (canonical_staff_access.py docstring + L54-71; the scope is set only by the aiohttp middleware at L156-198, which bot.py never installs). So the dossier asks K5/K8 to add a confirmation to a capability the P4-03 cutover already switched off, and "add the contract's confirmation, then remove the keyboard" is precisely the instruction under which an implementer re-wires a deliberately disabled mutation and books it as a safety improvement. An entry whose conditional approval can be discharged by reversing a fail-closed decision is more dangerous than one that says nothing. The same root error runs through the user-impact field, which narrates a folder walk the owner cannot currently perform and claims parity for "~18 capabilities" when six of the eighteen are already refusals or redirects and the marketing button lands in a preview whose body is the menu label.

G12.user_impact: Not "nobody notices". Only the shop card (S-204) plausibly survives looking the same; the other three change shape by their own rows' rationales. The profile card (S-205) stops being a card — its name/phone readout folds into the chat's identity affordance and its four chevron rows into settings. History (S-206) merges with AMyBookingsCard into one past/upcoming timeline, and the [service, date, sum] money column has to survive that merge. The staff card (S-212) merges with AMasterEarnCard into one earnings card with an expandable advice section, and the backend's wantsUpsell branch collapses with it — so the staff member does not see the same card either. The chips do not simply keep sitting under the composer: today the client surface re-fills them from a hard-coded default set after every MAYA answer (app.html L21669) and on an empty chat (L21593), so chips are never absent; server-driven chips mean any turn that returns none leaves the composer bare, a failure mode that does not exist today, and the staff cold-start chip «Записать клиента» navigates via __meGo('schedule') rather than sending text. Client-visible losses on S-239 are wider than "arbitrary URLs": the URL branch is tested first, before any action type, so any http/tel/mailto a message carries opens in a new window today; pruning the synonym sets (open_subs / open_subscriptions / subscription(s) / shop_subs …) also retires buttons already sitting in persisted chat history and still emitted by older server paths; and owners lose run_job, the only button that posts __runjob:<job> to the legacy chat endpoint. The two proactive cards (S-238) reach SaaS-tenant clients only — the legacy salon's clients never see them — and they do not fire "whenever the chat re-renders": each is a mount-time effect capped by a localStorage key (per tenant/user/balance for the loyalty offer, per last-visit signature for repeat booking). Moving them server-side changes when they appear and brings them under notify_prefs and quiet hours, which they bypass today. For the owner, the expense card (S-242) is neither a chat card nor a card left waiting: it mounts only when ?expenses=reminder|intake is in the URL (the Telegram deep link), keeps its source capsule in sessionStorage, and renders no cards until the owner presses «Получить сохранённые карточки». The pending approval is server state, so a reload loses the view, not the decision. The real owner-visible constraint is the frozen one: expenses.create is gap-keyed under GAP-EXPENSE-COMMIT and reaches no COMMIT on any widget kind, and "a missing mapping is a GAP, and a GAP has no button" — the successor can re-render the expense card but cannot carry its approve button until that gap is closed.
G12.security_impact: Direction is mixed, but two of the three risk claims are misattributed and the one improvement is understated. S-204: losing the self-hide guard is not by itself a cross-tenant catalogue leak — the tenant bootstrap already empties APP_DATA.subs/certs/services/masters on a foreign tenant ("Never show ME baked catalog / commerce on another salon", app.html ~L1037), so an unguarded card renders empty. The defect is that the scrub and the guard hang off the same client-set __ME_FOREIGN_TENANT / meIsMeTenant flags, computed inside a try/catch during tenant-config load, so there is no independent per-tenant fence today; the successor must derive tenant scope server-side rather than port either flag. S-206 is not a leak at all: AHistoryCard reads meCab().history only under meIsLegacy() and hands a non-legacy tenant a hard-coded empty list, so its gate protects truthfulness, not confidentiality — a merged timeline printing "no past visits" would assert an absence the system cannot know, because no tenant-scoped history API exists. The row the field omits is S-205: the profile card is the only surface showing which identity MAYA is acting as (legacy meCab().fullName/bookingPhone vs the SaaS me_saas_auth_v2:<ns> bundle user); its «клиент» line is a hard-coded literal, so it is an identity readout rather than an authority readout, but dissolving it still removes the client's only pre-command check of who MAYA thinks they are. S-242 points at the wrong control. The client's approve posts to /ai/approvals/{id}/{approve|reject} carrying payloadHash: card.payload_hash, and every decide is preceded by sameActor(), which re-reads /expense-intake/contexts and throws session_changed if tenant or user moved — those, not the card's four states, are the controls. The "executing" state is not a second-approve guard: the button stays live in that state and re-POSTs approve as «Повторить проверку результата» (app.html L33175), so double-approve safety already rests on server-side idempotency (approval id + payload hash). The merge requirement is therefore to carry the payload-hash binding and the same-actor precheck, and to treat the client expiry check as the presentational hint it is. The frozen limitations make this more fail-closed, not less: approval is role-gated with no separation-of-duties comparison (GAP-SEPARATION-OF-DUTIES open), STEP_UP_VERIFIED is unreachable so nothing can be raised to it, and expenses.create carries no COMMIT on any kind under GAP-EXPENSE-COMMIT — the successor withholds the button rather than weakening it. One row is a genuine improvement, larger than claimed: in S-239 the URL branch is tested before any action type, so a message payload carrying http/tel/mailto executes as window.open/__meExt, and run_job posts __runjob:<job> to the legacy chat endpoint — an LLM-authored payload can today both open an arbitrary external site and name a server-side job. Collapsing this to declared intents narrows both, but only once the intent vocabulary is closed and server-validated; until the gateway exists it is an intention, not a running fence. S-238 improves governance conditionally: the two cards bypass notify_prefs and quiet hours today, but their only frequency cap is a localStorage key (per tenant/user/balance; per last-visit signature), so a server pipeline without an equivalent dedupe would fire more often, not less.
G12.objection: The S-242 security claim inverts where the control lives, and that inversion would license exactly the wrong parity requirement in K6. The claim says "the expires_at check and the 'executing' state are the whole control against a second approve on an expired or in-flight money write." The code says otherwise: the current client does not block a second approve during 'executing' — `actionable` is `['pending','approved','executing'].includes(card.status) && (!expired || card.status!=='pending')`, and in the non-pending branch the same button re-POSTs `decide(card,'approve')` under the label «Повторить проверку результата» (app.html L33175). Double-approve safety therefore already rests on the server (`/ai/approvals/{id}/approve` bound to `payloadHash: card.payload_hash`, behind a `sameActor()` re-read of `/expense-intake/contexts` that throws `session_changed`). If K6 reviews the merge against the claim as written, it will protect a client state machine that is not a control and may drop the payload-hash binding and the same-actor precheck that are. Secondary: the group's proposed successor names — OFFER, PROFILE, LIST, ADVICE, CONFIRM — are not members of the contract's closed 22-kind enum (§2.1: CHOICE, SERVICE_SELECTOR, STAFF_SELECTOR, TIME_SLOT_SELECTOR, BOOKING_CONFIRMATION, SCHEDULE, CLIENT_LIST, METRIC, CHART, REPORT, STRATEGY_OPTIONS, APPROVAL, PROGRESS, LIMITATION, SOURCE_STATUS, SETTINGS_DRAFT, FORM, CONSENT_STATE, IDENTITY_BINDING, PAYMENT_HANDOFF, MEDIA_PREVIEW, ARTIFACT). So the reassuring premise — "what changes is only which declared contract kind backs each card" — cannot be checked against the contract at all, and for the expense row the mapping it names is blocked outright by GAP-EXPENSE-COMMIT. G12 also carries no entry in the dossier's CONDITIONAL GROUPS block despite being the group the same document flags as "contains the card that approves money"; the "flag for K6" wording in RECOMMENDED is not a condition that binds the signature.

G13.user_impact: Invisible for two of the seven rows, not five. Only S-613 and S-616 are backend-pinning plumbing (`?booking_backend` / `?booking_api_base` / `?booking_tenant` written into `me_booking_*` localStorage); every other row has a live external producer. First run is the loudest: after signup or login the app opens calendar setup via `?calendar_setup=1` (S-068, S-547), and the two producers pin different workspaces (`lgOpenAppCal` -> business/schedule vs `onbOpenApp` -> choose, which additionally clears `me_saas_workspace_v1:<ns>`), so a careless merge either stops opening calendar setup after onboarding or lands a just-onboarded owner in the wrong workspace; S-547 adds the failure mode this rebuild actually creates — a chat-driven in-app navigation replacing the full-page `location.replace` skips the `me_booking_*` write and the consumer boots with no backend base at all. S-618 is not plumbing: besides `?consent=1` it carries `?tips=<master>`, the post-visit tips push landing (maya-os-site L19115-19125), and `?device_id`, the VK OAuth return reader (L37654) — external producers (a push, an OAuth callback) that break silently if the merge treats app.html as canonical. S-617 is the staff-facing routing row, but the divergence is not between bundles: app.html and maya-os-site ship byte-identical `?cabinet` allow-lists — 8 values post-onboarding (app.html L6936, site L5656) and 11 values on the login route (app.html L38605, site L35673, the pair that adds `analytics`, `integrations`, `connect`). What decides whether those three stay reachable from a pasted link is reconciling the narrow list against the wide one, and that reconciliation has to be made in both copies. Nor is the `?promo` affordance the only deliberate loss: S-612's `?promo=1` forces the banner while `?promo=reset` deletes `promoNeverShow`/`promoShownOnce` outright — the "never show again" choice is erased, not overridden once — and the recommended booking-backend hardening additionally costs the app's own minted links, maya-site.html L245/L397 "Живое демо" and maya-admin.html L996/L1147 preview URLs, unless the successor keeps an allow-listed equivalent.
G13.security_impact: An improvement in direction, but today's state is worse than described and the danger sits in a different bundle than the text says. In app.html and maya-os-site the boot reader is host-gated (the public domain refuses `?booking_backend`/`?booking_api_base` and regex-validates the slug — app.html L795, site L628) while a second, UNGATED component-level reader persists the same values into localStorage. `app-tenant.html` (S-613) has no gate at all: no `isLocalDev`/`isPrivateHost` branch, no slug regex, only the ungated read at L6851-6870 — so "the boot-level reader is already gated" is false for precisely the bundle a tenant link to a salon owner opens. The token claim also lands on the wrong bundle: in app-tenant the Bearer comes from `ensureLocalSession()` (L7036), which auto-mints a throwaway booking client (`booking-<ts>@maya.local` with a hardcoded password) and POSTs those credentials plus the returned token to `localSaasApiBase` — a credential leak and a fully attacker-fed booking UI, but not an owner's session. The owner-session leak is S-616: maya-os-site drives the real SaaS session through the same base, including `saasRawRefresh` POSTing the long-lived REFRESH token to `localSaasApiBase + '/auth/refresh'` (L10080) and a Bearer `/auth/logout` (L10150), so one crafted link leaks more than an access token. The improvement is real only if the fix lands in all three bundles in the same pass and is an allow-list rather than a delete: the app mints these URLs itself (maya-site "Живое демо" L245/L397, maya-admin preview L996/L1147), so a blanket refusal breaks the owner's live preview and the public demo. Two smaller items: `?consent=1`, the 152-FZ consent force-show, exists in the superset site bundle (L22036), so a merge treating app.html as canonical silently drops a consent-gate entry point along with the `?device_id` OAuth-return reader (S-618); and `social_link_error` is echoed verbatim as UI copy on a trusted profile screen (`socialMessage = linkError`, app.html L34741; site L31392) — attacker-authored text usable for phishing, not an authority bypass. Nothing here touches server-side role decisions, and no frozen limitation (fail-closed 13/21, STEP_UP unreachable, Gate 10 measured not enforced, approval role-gated rather than separation-of-duties, GAP-ATTENDANCE-CONFIRM open) is affected either way.
G13.objection: The security field's load-bearing sentence is false for the bundle it singles out as most exposed. It asserts a uniform "gated boot + ungated component" structure across all three bundles, but `app-tenant.html` has no host gate and no slug validation whatsoever — grep for the public-domain branch present at app.html L795 and maya-os-site L628 returns nothing there; only the ungated read at L6851-6870 exists. The text then compounds the error by placing "a signed-in owner's token" in that same bundle, where the Bearer is actually an auto-minted throwaway booking account (`ensureLocalSession`, L7036, hardcoded password), while the genuine owner-session exposure — a long-lived refresh token POSTed to the attacker-named base at maya-os-site L10080 — is understated as an access token. Both errors push the reader's attention away from where the exploit is strongest, which is the failure mode this review exists to catch. Secondarily, the user-impact field's only concrete staff-facing claim is checkably wrong: the `?cabinet` allow-lists are byte-identical between the PWA and the public-site bundle, and the values it says are at stake (`analytics`, `integrations`, `connect`) are absent from the post-onboarding list in BOTH — so the stated mechanism (a PWA-vs-site divergence) does not exist, even though a real narrow-vs-wide reconciliation does.

G14.user_impact: Two of the three bundles are live and both have users who notice; only one row is genuinely invisible. (a) S-667 `app-tenant.html` is deployed at `/app/tenant-test.html`, but `saas_blueprint/CUTOVER_RUNBOOK.md` §0.3 defines it as a "тестовый фронт ОТДЕЛЬНЫМ файлом" whose rollback is deleting the file — a smoke-test front for the operator, not a client channel; the no-redirect hazard is real, but the people holding the link are testers, not clients. Its missing widget system (`grep -c meRenderWidgetCard` = 0 vs 2 in app.html) and missing governed settings are not a merge gap: the file is generated from app.html by `saas_blueprint/pg/tenantize_frontend.py` and is simply a stale generation (`__ME_SAAS_CTX` = 0 occurrences vs 150 in app.html), so re-running the generator restores those screens. The merge is not what "gives" them the widget chat. (b) S-240 `maya-os-site/index.html` is NOT invisible to every user. It is the same single-file app at build stamp `2026-08-01-crm-analytics-v2`, and `maya-saas-backend/deploy/platform/build-mayaos-edge.sh` copies it verbatim to the edge root `index.html`. Its own sibling rows say so: S-761 calls its push block "LIVE… a working notification control from a live tenant"; S-646 calls it "the ONLY live PWA that shows a client any policy text before they accept" (`setPrivacy(d.privacy_text || '')`, L22078); S-618 records `?consent` and `?device_id` deep links that only it carries. The implementation envelope's G10 exit criterion — "`maya-os-site/index.html` unreachable, probe recorded" (K15) — is the target state, not today's. Collapsing this bundle is visible: unless `privacy_text` rendering (grep: 1 there, 0 in app.html) and the `?consent` force-show are ported first, its users lose the policy screen they see today. (c) S-657 `privacy.html` is the one row where "nobody notices" holds — verified unreachable, the only repo reference is its own L4 self-instruction. But the successor wording "privacy.html becomes the served policy text the consent widget already reads" is false today: app.html's AMayaConsent renders no policy text at all (`privacy_text` grep = 0); the widget has to be taught to read it, and the file has to actually be published.
G14.security_impact: Not an improvement in consent-record consistency — that part is neutral — and a real capability check is at risk. (1) There is one consent writer today, not two. `webhook_server.py:4796 consent_submit_handler` is an A18 initiator that performs no local write; `legacy_client_command_bridge.py` states "No phone/User resolution, local consent write, or mutating fallback" and forwards to `http://127.0.0.1:3107/api/internal/legacy/client-commands/consent` — the same NestJS Client-consent boundary app.html reaches directly via `/client-channel/consent` (`customers.controller.ts:74 submitLegacyNativeConsent`). G16.user_impact: The client is who notices, and the diagnosis of today's dead end holds — but the promised payoff does not. Verified as stated: a walk-up client who scans the printed chair QR lands on tips.html?master=<slug> (generate_tip_qrs.py encodes exactly that), picks a master and an amount, and can then do nothing. isConfigured() (tips.html L1243) requires sbpPhone with >=10 digits AND a non-empty sbpBank; all five masters in tips-data.js ship both empty while all five carry a populated bankAppUrl, so the five copy buttons and "Я перевёл" are disabled (L1366) and even "Открыть банк" is disabled (L1370-1378, gated on `configured &&` despite the URL existing), with "реквизиты не заполнены" on every master (L1327). What is NOT true is that the merge makes the payment hand-off complete for the first time. GAP-TIPS is open (ownerState "none", closedAt null), and under the certified contract PAY.5 tips are a payment-class capability following PAY.1-PAY.4; PAY.4 says that while no payment-class owner is registered the emission carries capability_gap_ref, a null commit_intent and a null continue_intent and "states in text that the purchase cannot be completed in the product yet — a gap-blocked commit renders as prose, never as a disabled-styled button". R3.3.1 additionally makes BUTTON → EXTERNAL PROVIDER unconstructible, so bankAppUrl cannot travel into the widget at all, and AE_FAMILY_FLOOR sets money: STEP_UP_VERIFIED, a level frozen as unreachable. So the contract-declared successor replaces a disabled button with prose; it does not deliver a completed hand-off, and masters do not start seeing tips arrive from this route on the strength of this signature. Two further corrections: signing G16 changes no deployed byte (dossier §5), and the dead end is in any case a one-line data-or-gating fix to a live static page that needs no merge to land — the working sibling path (app.html L22213 __tipsSend → L10655 meTipsPaymentURL) already completes the hand-off with no SBP data. Finally, the real user-facing risk this group carries is the opposite of the one claimed: S-170 is the anonymous, session-less, no-install QR landing, and a chat-first successor behind a SESSION_VERIFIED floor would kill exactly the flow the printed stickers serve — S-170's own parityRiskNote says so, and the dossier's conditional for G16 records only the wording constraint, not the preservation of the anonymous entry.
G16.security_impact: The direction is wrong in both halves. First half: it is true that S-170 today is roleMode "any", makes no network call and carries no session, token or role check, so no client-side check is being removed that a server-side check must replace — but the conclusion "neutral" is wrong, because the successor ADDS an authority floor where none existed (money family floor STEP_UP_VERIFIED, frozen unreachable) and removes an external-provider button the contract forbids outright (R3.3.1). That is a hardening plus an availability loss for the anonymous walk-up, not neutrality. Second half is inverted and must be struck: folding "Я перевёл" into a server-backed widget would NOT "create the first persisted record of a claim the system never witnessed". That record already existed — POST /api/tips/sent wrote database.save_tip and fired a Telegram alert ("Клиент отметил перевод чаевых") plus web push from an endpoint with no auth whatsoever, caller-supplied master/amount/record_id (SECURITY_AUDIT_2026-06-22_DEEP.md:400-407) — and it has already been retired: webhook_server.py tip_sent_handler now returns 410 "tip_signal_retired" with payment_confirmed:false, business_mutations:0, under the marker p5_b22_unverified_tip_signal_retired. B22 Option A (RECOMMENDED) is explicit: "Durable tip fact: no", "Staff notification: none", no canonical tip owner in Maya V1. So prescribing that the claim "must be stored and rendered as a client assertion" is not a safety caveat — it would reverse a decision the repo has already implemented and re-create a spoofable, unauthenticated staff-notification primitive. The correct constraint is stronger than GAP-ATTENDANCE-CONFIRM shape: while GAP-TIPS is open there is no durable tip fact and no button at all, only gap prose (PAY.4/PAY.5). Third claim also struck: the merge does not mandate placing masters' personal SBP phone numbers into tips-data.js. Publishing those numbers is one bad way to fix the dead end, not a consequence of the disposition. Worth recording instead, and unmentioned by the entry: tips-data.js already publishes five per-master YClients tip tokens (the bankAppUrl UUIDs) in an unauthenticated static script (L1178) — an existing exposure the contract-declared successor would actually remove.
G16.objection: The entry's central promise is the exact outcome the certified contract forbids. G17.security_impact: No authority or tenant-isolation change — but the original's stated mechanism is wrong, and that matters because it is the sentence licensing "NONE". `window.__meAuthReq` is not a server-side gate: at app-tenant.html:22381-22392 it is a client-side credential builder that returns null only when localStorage holds no Telegram initData, no `tg_auth_data` and no `web_session_token`. The conclusion still holds — the client never decides the role, `Notification.permission` is a browser-OS gate that was never an authority check, nothing load-bearing is removed and no new server-side authority check is required — with one tightening: the recorded answer is itself new server-side state, so "nothing server-side has to replace it" is true of the authority check, not of the record. G17.objection: The load-bearing error is "Someone already on app.html or the MAYA OS bundle notices essentially nothing… what retires is a third copy of them, not a capability." That is false on the group's own headline defect: `__meMaybePush` arms the same one-shot `document.addEventListener('pointerdown', once, {once:true})` → `Notification.requestPermission()` in all three bundles (app-tenant:22745, app.html:40736, maya-os-site:37565). So the entry describes a real behaviour change for every bundle's users as no change at all — the "neutral claimed where something moves" failure mode — and it lets the group read as a one-bundle defect when it is a three-bundle one, which is precisely what the parity condition has to cover. Second, "the subscribe path already gates on a server-side session (`window.__meAuthReq`)" attributes the gate to a client-side localStorage credential builder; the actual server gate is verified-Client-only and rejects the web-session channel entirely, so the current state is both safer and more broken than described. Contingent: signing removes nothing, so there is no security delta in this wave — the gain arrives only if K16 executes.
